public_rationale: The September court order documents six pending actions, including consolidated cases. A contemporaneous inventory adds Raw Story and The Intercept. Even grouping the consolidated author and newspaper actions, the records establish at least five pending proceedings. That supports the ordinary reading of many lawsuits pending.
limitations: Five is an evaluator-supplied threshold, not a number Marcus stated.
The two additional cases rely on a dated specialist compilation because accessible primary records were not obtained.
This is a lower bound, not a complete litigation census.
Pending lawsuits establish legal exposure, not liability or the merits of their allegations.

our_interpretation: OpenAI or its operating affiliates must be defendants in a substantial plurality of unresolved civil actions.
Use at least five distinct pending actions as a conservative operational reading of many. Count actions rather than plaintiffs, allegations, or motions.
Report consolidation explicitly and check that the conclusion also holds when consolidated actions are grouped.
For this ongoing observation, use public litigation status during September 1–25, 2024, ending at publication.
criteria.support_condition: Court records and reliable contemporaneous status reporting establish at least five distinct pending actions against OpenAI.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A sufficiently complete litigation inventory establishes fewer than five pending actions, with the purported additional actions dismissed, concluded, duplicated, or directed at other defendants.
